sents.zh: 中国人很早就觉得写字是一件很美的事。
sents.en: Chinese people early on felt that writing was a beautiful thing.

sents.zh: 一千六百多年以前，有一个很有名的人。
sents.en: More than sixteen hundred years ago there was a very famous man.

sents.zh: 他很小的时候就开始学写字。
sents.en: He began learning to write when he was very young.

sents.zh: 他每天都练习，一天也没有停过。
sents.en: He practised every day, and never stopped for a single day.

sents.zh: 写完字以后，他就去水边洗笔。
sents.en: After writing he would go to the water’s edge to wash his brush.

sents.zh: 因为他洗了很多年，所以那里的水都变黑了。
sents.en: Because he did this for so many years, the water there turned black.
The characters he wrote were extremely beautiful.

sents.zh: 有的字像风，有的字像水。
sents.en: Some were like wind, some like water.
So people called him the Sage of Calligraphy.

sents.zh: 有一年，他和很多朋友在山里见面。
sents.en: One year he met many friends in the mountains.

sents.zh: 那天天气很好，大家一边喝一边写诗。
sents.en: The weather that day was fine, and they drank and wrote poems.

sents.zh: 他把大家的诗放在一起，还写了几句话。
sents.en: He gathered everyone’s poems together and wrote a few lines of his own.

sents.zh: 那几句话成了中国最有名的字。
sents.en: Those few lines became the most famous writing in China.

sents.zh: 到今天，还有很多人在学他写字的方法。
sents.en: To this day many people still study his way of writing.
